title: The social room as evidence: who is present, absent, allowed, believed, and interrupted

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0018 social-room / kinship-conflict layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no legal/family-therapy/safeguarding authority.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, and seed-cue factoring during rev0018
limitations: Public sources support orientation, vocabulary, and review routing only; they do not supply consented bedside detail.
Social-room material is high risk for identifiability, blame, gossip, living-family harm, and legal overreach.
Records must not advise treatment, family conflict resolution, safeguarding steps, legal authority, or institutional procedure.

moment.plain_scene: Around a dying person, the room has a social map: who is at the bedside, who waits outside, who is phoned, who is not told, who is believed, who is treated as family, and who is invisible.
ordinary_language_queries: who is allowed in the room when dying
who counts as family at end of life

content_layers.observation_text: Around a dying person, the room has a social map: who is at the bedside, who waits outside, who is phoned, who is not told, who is believed, who is treated as family, and who is invisible.
content_layers.source_synthesis: National Academies caregiving material, family-meeting literature, and end-of-life ethics sources all support the idea that patient, family, and care-team interests are entangled but not identical.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: For DeathVocab, the social room is not background; it changes who can witness, speak, decide, touch, remember, be believed, and be harmed.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Render as observed social grammar and boundary language only; never as family therapy, legal advice, safeguarding instruction, or moral verdict.

what_this_is_not: a legal determination of next of kin or authority
a judgment about whether a family loved the dying person enough
uncertainties: Public sources can name the social pattern, but only consented accounts can supply the room texture.
Local law, facility policy, culture, family history, and patient preference may change what the record means.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A reader may recognize that what hurt was not only the death but the room’s map of permission, recognition, exclusion, and interruption.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future practitioner review should ask how teams name family roles without freezing or judging them.
language_notes: Avoid pathologizing disagreement as denial unless a source and reviewer justify the term.
Do not turn one family role into the moral center of the death.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0018 from public-source synthesis and seed-cue factoring; no private account, no clinical validation, no legal validation, no public release.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not admit names, rare details, unique family configurations, private conflict, or living-person accusations without explicit consent and harm review.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record to decide treatments, transfers, hospice, medications, nutrition, hydration, or level of care.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer authority, next-of-kin status, visitation rights, surrogate rules, reporting duties, or document validity from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not generalize a family pattern into a tradition or ritual rule; route tradition-specific material to tradition-holder review.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical advice or a substitute for the local care team; symptom, capacity, delirium, safety, and medication issues require qualified review.
safety_notes: Protect living family members as living people, not as characters in a death story.
Avoid voyeurism around conflict, money, sexuality, estrangement, substance use, abuse, and secrecy.
Use enough context to prevent flattening, but not enough to identify anyone.
